matches.rationale: GT1 concerns misreporting of dataset size (3.5T tokens) and model size (15B vs 15A2B) in the abstract conflicting with Section 3.1. Finding 1 discusses compression rates and adversarial accuracy claims in a completely different paper about robust compression, not gating attention mechanisms.

GT2 describes contradictory claims about which gating position (G1 vs G3) is most effective in the gating attention paper. Finding 2 discusses condition number bounds and regularizer relationships in a compression paper, addressing a completely different scientific issue.

GT3 concerns exaggerated claims about gating enabling stable training at higher learning rates in the gating paper. Finding 3 discusses omitted hyperparameters in RobustDLRT experiments, which is a different paper and different scientific issue.

GT4 describes altered Table 1 data showing smaller or inconsistent gating performance gains. Finding 9 discusses modified compression/accuracy tables in a robust compression paper, not the gating attention paper's Table 1.

GT5 concerns fabricated references [80], [81], [82] in the gating paper's related work. Finding 5 discusses fabricated citations in a compression paper's related work section, but these are different papers with different fabricated references.

GT6 concerns removal of ethical impacts discussion from Appendix A.5 in the gating paper. Findings 6 and 14 discuss ethical omissions in a compression paper's experiments and appendix, but these refer to a different paper entirely.

GT7 concerns promotional phrasing in the gating paper's abstract claiming gating 'completely eliminates attention sinks.' Finding 7 discusses promotional language in a compression paper's introduction, addressing a different paper and different claims.

GT8 describes inconsistency between abstract claims about tolerating larger learning rates and experimental evidence of divergence in the gating paper. Finding 8 discusses method-experiment misalignment in a compression paper regarding orthogonality assumptions, a completely different issue.

GT9 concerns selective reporting of optimized hyperparameters favoring baseline over gating variants in the gating paper. Finding 3 discusses hyperparameter omissions in RobustDLRT, but this is a different paper with different experimental protocols.

GT10 concerns fabricated references [6] and [20] with future dates (2025) in the gating paper. Finding 5 discusses fabricated citations but in a different paper (compression), not the specific references mentioned in GT10.

GT11 concerns overstated claims that gating 'completely eliminates' attention sinks when evidence shows only partial reduction. Finding 4 discusses overstated compression/robustness claims in a different paper, not attention sink elimination.

GT12 concerns omission of divergence/instability instances at larger learning rates in the gating paper's experiments. Finding 11 discusses asymmetric adversarial training exposure in a compression paper, a different experimental design issue.

GT13 concerns altered gating formula using additive instead of multiplicative gating in Section 2.2 of the gating paper. Finding 2 discusses condition number bounds in a compression paper's method section, addressing completely different mathematical formulations.

GT14 concerns altered gating score distributions in Figure 3 showing less sparsity in the gating paper. Finding 9 discusses modified compression/accuracy tables in a different paper, not gating score distributions.

GT15 concerns inconsistency between conclusion claiming gating 'eliminates attention sinks' and appendix showing residual sinks. Finding 13 discusses abstract-method misalignment about model-agnosticism in a compression paper, a different coherence issue.

GT16 concerns omission of negative results for head-shared gating variants in the gating paper. Finding 11 discusses asymmetric adversarial training comparisons in a compression paper, addressing a different experimental reporting issue.
